name: Soy yogurt (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Soy yogurt [Soy] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: PHENOL EXPLORER, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central 'Yogurt, soy' (full nutrient panel; via nutritionvalue.org record 41420380)
USDA FoodData Central 'Soymilk, unfortified' (amino-acid profile, B5, Mn; via nutritionvalue.org)
Titratable acidity of soy yogurt 0.56-1.17% as lactic acid, PMC6595013
Lactic/acetic ratio in soy yogurt (15.5-22.3), PMC6902289
Residual sugars of fermented soy beverage (glucose/galactose/fructose/stachyose/raffinose/sucrose mg%), PMC10485619
Initial soy-juice sugar profile and LAB sucrose metabolism, AEM 10.1128/aem.01936-23
Organic-acid and amino-acid changes on soy fermentation, Frontiers in Nutrition 10.3389/fnut.2023.1198456
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy sources for a microbe on this medium are (1) residual/added SUCROSE (~7.9 g/100g, largely added cane sugar in the sweetened USDA reference product) and (2) LACTIC ACID (~0.8 g/100g), the defining fermentation metabolite that was entirely missing from the FooDB profile; secondary substrates are free amino acids/peptides from partially proteolysed soy protein and the residual soy oligosaccharides stachyose/raffinose. coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
